title: Column comparison for total complexes with finitely many rows
statement: Let C be an abelian category [def-sp-abelian], K and L nonnegative double complexes [def-sp-double-complex-total], f:K→L a morphism, and N a natural number. Assume K^{p,q} and L^{p,q} are zero for every p and every q>N. Assume that for every q the horizontal complex map K^{•,q}→L^{•,q}, equivalently the q-th component of the flipped map, is a quasi-isomorphism. Then the canonical total map Tot(f) is a quasi-isomorphism.

source.place: Section 12.25, the second filtration by vertical degree; finite filtration comparison

proof.text: For q=0,...,N+1 let F^q Tot(K) consist of the summands with vertical degree at least q, and similarly for L. The horizontal differential preserves q and the vertical differential raises it, so these are subcomplexes. F^{N+1} is zero by the support hypothesis, while F^0 is the full total. Each short exact sequence 0→F^{q+1}→F^q→gr^q→0 splits in every degree by the direct sum decomposition of the diagonal.

The quotient gr^q has degree-m object K^{m-q,q}, with zero terms if m<q. Its differential is the horizontal differential; the vertical differential lands in F^{q+1} and disappears. Hence the quotient map is the extension by zero of the horizontal map in degree q, translated by q; it is a quasi-isomorphism by the hypothesis. Equivalently, extend both indices to integers, transpose, and apply HomologicalComplex₂.total.quasiIso_map_of_finitely_many_columns for the outer bounds 0 and N, transporting along totalization and extension identifications.

Induct downwards on q from N+1. The map on F^{N+1} is a quasi-isomorphism because both sides are zero. If the map on F^{q+1} is a quasi-isomorphism, its map and the quotient map are quasi-isomorphisms; the long exact homology sequences of the two short exact sequences give a quasi-isomorphism on F^q by the five lemma (the existing HomologicalComplex.HomologySequence.quasiIso_τ₂). At q=0 this is the asserted total map. This includes N=0 and requires no horizontal upper bound.

proof_origin.place: Finite filtration argument; details of the five-lemma induction written by E1
